newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate drops to 6.5/7.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate drops to 6.5/7.0 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 6.5/7.0 percent from a high of 8.0 percent on expectations of lower rates at the end of the week due to return of some funds, dealers said on Wednesday.
There will be a maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit on Friday.
"People are expecting rates to come off on Friday because of the bill maturity," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
A large local bank was earlier seen borrowing overnight funds at 7.7/8 percent. "That's a bit surprising as the bank has recently been lending," the dealer said.
In the morning, interbank rates were generally steady as the market remained short of funds, dealers said.
One-month money was at 8.1/2 percent against 8.0 percent on Tuesday.
Three-month money was unchanged at 8.0/1 percent, while one-week was flat at 8.0 percent.
Dealers said absence of central Bank Negara Malaysia in the market also kept rates firm.

Bank Negara has been injecting funds over the past two weeks to help ease market tightness, caused by its massive intervention in the foreign exchange market to defend the ringgit against speculative attack.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were slightly up on expectations of a softening in interbank rates.
At 0800 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.42, or an implied yield of 7.58 percent.
The December contract was unchanged at 92.64, or 7.36 percent while March 1998 contract was up one point to 92.74, or 7.26 percent.
